method: Read-only review of the complete runtime diff, added tests, persistence/repair callers, copied QA version changes and release workflow according to review-agent. Self-review by the implementation agent, not independent.
resolvedFindings: Preserve healthy pistons when loading a saved failure in a newly separated component.
Keep inactive piston-only faults through rotary swaps without affecting the rotary engine.
Respect pump and ignition failure in recovery, tuning and restoration warm starts and in NOS output.
Exclude exhaust pumping work from extra motor/oil friction heat.
Update both saved and diagnostic release versions and copied browser expectations.
visualCheck: Desktop and 390-pixel service screenshots inspected: labels, fault summary and isolated replacement controls are readable.
limits: Fictional lumped component calibration, shared thermal nodes and proportional wear; no certified real-car or finite-element model.
Timing loss uses misfires, valve-contact damage and combustion cut, not a new tooth-by-tooth chain solver. Exhaust restriction uses dissipative native shaft load, not modified pipe geometry.
No supercharger in the tuning catalogue yet; visible engine bay, mounting and removal remain later phases.

Final HTML covers tuning, saves, new runs and diagnosis. Component service buttons additionally use original VehiclePanel/CarPhysics in a local module fixture, not a full workshop-drive/main-service-timer scenario.
Multiplayer uses local independent browser processes with public PeerJS/WebRTC; no separate-PC, mobile or restrictive NAT/TURN validation.
No physical controller or subjective listening test. CPU sample excludes world/GPU/AI/audio.
